query_security_property: Untrusted data from servlet request inputs, environment variables, or system properties must not flow to generic writer/output operations or filesystem-path construction/write operations without appropriate escaping, encoding, or canonicalization.
hard_coded_sinks: Writer/PrintWriter/Appendable print/write/append; File/Paths/Files and java.io path-based operations
hard_coded_security_assumption: CWE-116 is approximated as generic untrusted-data-to-output/filesystem taint flow.
template_pattern: untrusted input -> writer/output or filesystem path
hypothesis_status: CANDIDATE_ONLY: must compare against per-case actual encoding/escaping mechanisms before concluding collapse

query_security_property: A public web-exposed endpoint that invokes a name-matched sensitive operation should contain an explicit security annotation or an authorization-check call.
hard_coded_sources: Public Spring/JAX-RS/Micronaut-style mapped methods or HttpServlet doGet/doPost/service
hard_coded_sinks: Calls with names suggesting delete/create/update user, role/permission changes, execute/eval, credential/secret/token access, upload/download, configure, start/stop, etc.
hard_coded_security_assumption: Improper access control is approximated as missing explicit authorization around sensitive operations in web endpoints.
template_pattern: web endpoint -> sensitive operation, with no explicit authorization evidence
hypothesis_status: STRONG_CANDIDATE: supervisor specifically hypothesizes this template may collapse heterogeneous CWE-284 mechanisms

query_security_property: User-controlled HTTP/request or multipart filename data should not flow into filesystem write, move, transfer, or file-path operations.
hard_coded_security_assumption: Unrestricted file upload is approximated as user-controlled request/upload data reaching a filesystem destination.
template_pattern: request/upload filename -> filesystem write or move
hypothesis_status: CANDIDATE_ONLY: must compare against per-case authorization, extension/type/content, path, and sanitizer mechanisms

query_security_property: A user-controlled request identifier should not flow into an identifier-like parameter of a resource access or modification method.
hard_coded_sinks: Arguments mapped to parameters named like id/uuid/guid/key in get/find/select/query/delete/remove/update/edit/set methods
hard_coded_security_assumption: IDOR is approximated as generic taint from user-controlled identifier to an ID-like resource-operation parameter.
template_pattern: user-controlled ID -> ID-like resource access/modification parameter
hypothesis_status: STRONG_CANDIDATE: relational ownership/authenticated-user context is not represented by the generic taint template
